method='table'|'bisection' implemented; run_simulation calls prepare_hooks before load_energyplus_api (runner.py:136-137; pyenergyplus is imported lazily); prepare() warms set_tmp with the three call shapes of the bisection (numba sees the same types in prepare and in the callbacks, for both postures); tdb = tr (equal_air) and the air temperature with the MRT of the zone (zone) are bisected correctly; SET_<zone> is the SET of the previous-timestep MAT/MRT/RH; MAT/MRT/RH outputs at the ACCIS frequencies; set_of_results; sitting by default at ≤ 1.2 met; A6-1..A6-4 closed in code and docs. add_thermal_comfort_model is correct and the measurement is reproducible, and ta, tr, RH, clo and v are exactly Pierce's inputs (validated), but met is not: EnergyPlus's Pierce converts the activity level with 1.8258 m² while E-F1 (and the hooks) use 1.8 m², which alone raises the SET by ~0.1 K, the size of the reported differences. Moreover the EnergyPlus 25.1/25.2 code omits the activity term 5.66·(met − 0.85)^0.39 of the real-environment hc (the Engineering Reference and the decision say it is there; pythermalcomfort has it); the sample's 110.7 W/person is just below the ≈1.046 met at which it acts, so the '0.2 K standing / 0.35 K sitting' agreement does not generalize: at 1.1-1.2 met the two SETs are expected to differ by ~0.4-1 K.

Comfort standard 24 is a thin layer on the bisection hook as decided: band 19.09/28.18 °C from (∓tsv_limit + 2.6)/0.11, neutral 23.6 ± set_offset (K of SET), 0.7/1.0 with an extrapolation warning, other limits and modes 0/3 raise ValueError, categories 80/90 → 0.5, tr_mode='zone' Top = (ta + tr_prev)/2, B5 minimum after the inversion and a once-per-zone 18 °C warning without minimum, People inputs (activity/104.76, clothing schedule or dynamic output, air velocity schedule), TSV_causal and HoursInCausalBand (occupied, band inclusive), Pierce added, rejected by AddAccis/modify_accis/EMS code/GUI/prompts, TODO P2 for the Erl fallback. Issues: apply_set_setpoints(clo=None) with the dynamic clothing model makes EnergyPlus stop (no Fanger/Pierce/KSU); a prepared model runs silently without its hook; stale outputs when the hook skips a zone; the SET of the hook against Pierce depends on met (see E-F1).

findings.location: tests/core/test_pierce_set.py:141 (met = activity/(58.2*1.8)); accim/sim/comfort_hooks.py:169 (MET_ACTIVITY_LEVEL = 58.2*PMV_BODY_SURFACE_AREA, used by SetSetpointHook.zone_inputs at :942); notes/decisions.md:500-509 (E-F1: '1.8 m²', 'met=activity schedule/(58.2·1.8)'); docs/source/4_detailed use.md:1608 (SET_Act_<zone>: 'the body surface area of 1.8 m² with which EnergyPlus gives the activity per person')
findings.problem: E-F1 does not use EnergyPlus's input for the metabolic rate: the Pierce model of EnergyPlus converts the activity level with BodySurfAreaPierce = 1.8258 m² (ThermalComfort.hh:69; ThermalComfort.cc 25.1:824 and 25.2:849, ActLevel = activityLevelSched/BodySurfAreaPierce), while 1.8 m² (BodySurfArea) is used only by Fanger and KSU (25.1:570 and :1460). The comparison (and the SET hooks that F1 compares with Pierce) use met = activity/(58.2·1.8), 1.43 % higher (1.0567 against 1.0418 met for 110.7 W/person). The reported differences (−0.045 K standing, −0.116 K sitting; F1 −0.08/−0.155 K) therefore mix an input mismatch with the model differences, while the decision and the docs attribute them to the posture and the model only; the statement that the body area 'does not change them' refers only to the body_surface_area argument of set_tmp (heat storage), not to the met conversion.
findings.evidence: A pure-Python transcription of CalcStandardEffectiveTemp (EnergyPlus 25.1) fed with the timestep outputs of a yearly run of the sample model with Pierce (Seville, 6 timesteps/h, Zone Mean Air/Radiant Temperature, Zone Air Relative Humidity, site pressure, schedules) and met = activity/(58.2·1.8258) reproduces 'Zone Thermal Comfort Pierce Model Standard Effective Temperature' within 0.00098/0.00073 K per timestep (52 560 timesteps per zone; 0.00016 K hourly), which confirms the 1.8258 m². With met = activity/(58.2·1.8) the same algorithm gives a SET higher by +0.096 K on average over the year (hourly +0.057 to +0.142 K; +0.082 K at 0.5 clo, +0.110 K at 1.0 clo), the size of the reported differences: with matched met, pythermalcomfort would be roughly 0.1 K further below EnergyPlus than reported.
findings.fix: Re-run E-F1 with met = activity/(58.2·1.8258) (the input of the Pierce model) and update notes/decisions.md (E-F1 and F1 entries), docs 4.9.2/4.9.3, CHANGELOG and MEASURED in tests/core/test_pierce_set.py, reporting separately the effect of accim's 1.8 m² convention. Ask the author whether the SET hooks (SetSetpointHook.zone_inputs, Sun2026SetpointHook) should convert with 1.8258 m² (consistent with the Pierce SET that F1 and F3 report beside them) or keep 1.8 m² (the ISO 7730/Fanger convention) with the ~0.1 K offset documented; correct 'the body surface area of 1.8 m² with which EnergyPlus gives the activity per person' (true for Fanger and KSU, not for Pierce).

findings.location: notes/decisions.md:500-501 and :530-534 (E-F1 context and consequences), :488-493 (F1 consequences); docs/source/4_detailed use.md:1615 and :1648; tests/core/test_pierce_set.py and tests/core/test_sun2026_set.py (one activity level, 110.7 W/person)
findings.problem: The description of EnergyPlus's Pierce model on which the comparison is judged (hc = max(8.6·v^0.53, 5.66·(met − 0.85)^0.39) with v ≥ 0.137 m/s, from the Engineering Reference 25.2 §19.1.4, eqs. 19.27-19.28, pp. 1567-1568) is not what EnergyPlus 25.1/25.2 computes: CalcStandardEffectiveTemp uses, in the real environment, Hc = max(3.0·P^0.53, 8.600001·(v·P)^0.53) with v ≥ 0.1 m/s (25.1:888 and :918-920) and applies 5.66·(ActMet − 0.85)^0.39 only to the standard environment (StdHc, 25.1:1108, 25.2:1144), whereas pythermalcomfort's ASHRAE 55 code adds it to the real environment (two_nodes_gagge.py:343-345, unless calculate_ce). The term exceeds 3.0 W/m²K above ≈1.046 met; the sample model's 110.7 W/person is 1.042 met in the Pierce model, just below it, so E-F1's 'within 0.2 K standing and 0.35 K sitting' and F1's −0.08/−0.155 K hold only near 1.0 met and do not carry over to the 1.1-1.2 met of block F §2.3 or of typical offices, where the SET of the hooks and the Pierce SET that F1 reports beside it will differ by several tenths of a kelvin to more than 1 K (≈0.1 of TSV per K).
findings.evidence: EnergyPlus 25.1, sample model with its activity schedules set to 130 W/person (1.223 met in Pierce), one year: the transcription WITHOUT the activity term reproduces the Pierce output within 0.0005 K; WITH the term the SET is 1.09 K lower on average (max 1.55 K). On the conditions of the 110.7 W run, adding the term changes EnergyPlus's SET by 0 K at 1.042 met, −0.39 K (−0.24 to −0.57) at 1.1 met and −0.97 K (−0.65 to −1.37) at 1.2 met. A proxy of the hook's inputs at 130 W (met/1.8, radiative fraction 0.73, the activity term, EnergyPlus's algorithm) is 1.04 K below the Pierce output on average (−0.66 to −1.53 K). set_tmp itself could not be run (numba blocked), so the pythermalcomfort figures at 1.1-1.2 met are estimates.
findings.fix: Repeat the E-F1 measurement at 1.1 and 1.2 met (e.g. 115 and 126 W/person) and both clothing levels, record the differences by activity level in decisions.md and docs 4.9.2/4.9.3, and restrict the present statements to ≈1.0 met; document that EnergyPlus's code (which cites ASHRAE 55-2017 Appendix D) omits the activity-dependent hc of the real environment, contrary to its Engineering Reference, while pythermalcomfort includes it; parametrize test_pierce_set.py over the activity level; the author decides, together with open question #9, which SET is the reference of F1 and F3 (and whether to report the code/documentation mismatch to EnergyPlus).

findings.problem: Because T_rm_in is the running mean of the zone's own operative temperature, clipping BOTH setpoints to T_rm_in +/- delta drags the inactive setpoint to the free-floating temperature: the dead band collapses to <= delta_heat + delta_cool (2 K), heating or cooling run to hold the zone within 1 K of its own recent mean (also on unoccupied days), the hour counters measure that 2 K band, and the exposure can drift by only about (1-alpha)*delta = 0.2 K/day while the zone is held in the window, a far stricter and different control than 'rate' (0.5 K/day on the setpoints, full band).
